18. <u>Spills and Leaks</u>. The accidental spilling or leakage of fluids such as DFA may cause significant, but very local, impact on the snow surface, firn and ice. It is extremely unlikely that the DFA will contaminate the core hole, or the sea should the hole be accidentally opened at the base, because this fluid mixture has a lower density than seawater. It will be pumped out, although the pumping operation will probably leave traces behind, and returned to McMurdo Station.
During the 1976-77 drilling operation there will be no attempt made for deep core drilling into the bottom sdeiments. It is anticipated that this attempt will be made during the 1977-78 austral summer. The possibility of encountering hydrocarbon traces during this drilling has been considered.
The geologic structure under the Ross Ice Shelf is not known. Studies from shipboard in the open Ross Sea indicate the presence of some structures which could be considered as potential hydrocarbon traps. Whether or not these structures extend beneath the Ross Ice Shelf as far south as the drill site is not known.
Explosion seismology is the only reliable technique capable of obtaining adequate subsurface sediment and bedrock data for a detailed interpretation of the geology. However, because of problems of energy transfer across the ice-water interface if this survey is conducted from the surface of the Ross Ice Shelf the technique will yield poor and probably useless data.
